name: Jonas of Bobbio
knownFor: Monk of Bobbio who wrote the Life of Columbanus, the Irish founder of Luxeuil and Bobbio. Later, as an abbot, he wrote the Life of John of Réomé.
dates: Entered Bobbio three years after Columbanus's death, Dana Munro says. Wrote the Life of Columbanus about 640, by Bruno Krusch's date, before 642. An abbot in the third year of King Clothar, which Krusch reckons as 659. No held source gives his birth year or his death
place: Born at Susa in Italy, at the foot of the Alps, say the Acta Sanctorum editors G. Henschenius and D. Papebrochius. A monk of Bobbio; with Bishop Amand on the Scheldt and the marsh of the Elnone; at Réomé, on his way to Chalon

keyWorks.title: Life of Columbanus
keyWorks.about: written at Abbot Bertulf's command, from the stories of the saint's companions and of the abbots Attala and Eustasius. Its preface is addressed to the abbots Waldebert and Bobolenus

keyWorks.title: Life of John of Réomé
keyWorks.about: written at the request of the monks of Réomé, during a journey ordered by King Clothar and Queen Balthild. Bruno Krusch says two forgers of the Carolingian age reworked it

keyWorks.title: Life of Eustasius
keyWorks.about: the Life of Columbanus's pupil and abbot of Luxeuil. Giovanni Domenico Mansi quotes its account of the council of Mâcon

traces: Bruno Krusch says the later Lives of John of Réomé were built on Jonas's book. One forger claimed to have lived before Jonas. Another claimed he wrote from men who had often seen John.
Krusch finds a prologue like Jonas's, and a phrase Jonas often used, in a Life of Bibianus of Saintes. He places its language in the Carolingian age.
remembered: Dana Munro, his translator, says almost all accounts of the Irish missionaries are lost, so this Life of Columbanus is of great value.
Munro holds that the Life reflects the companions' feelings faithfully and often keeps the saint's own words. He adds that, as in such Lives, its miracles are many.
Laurentius Surius, in a heading Vincentius Barralis prints, calls Jonas an abbot and a contemporary of Columbanus.

uncertain: Whether he wrote the older Life of Vedast, bishop of Arras. Krusch believes so, from its style and a wonder told in nearly the same words. He says Louis Duchesne agreed, and later G. Kurth. The Life itself names no author.
His own life is known mostly from his prefaces and the opening of his Life of John. Dana Munro, Bruno Krusch and the Acta Sanctorum editors add a little.
His origin. The Acta Sanctorum editors say he was Italian, not Irish, and born at Susa. They rest this on their Life of Attala, which is not held.
Whether he was abbot of Bobbio. The Acta Sanctorum editors list him after Bobolenus among its abbots, with a perhaps. The Réomé opening calls him abbot but names no house.
Munro's translation leaves out the preface. Its Latin is held only in a hard-to-read copy of Vincentius Barralis's book of 1613.
